name: Corporate Creations
old_description: Established in 1995 and based right here in Omaha Nebraska, Corporate Creations specializes in custom screen printing, embroidery and promotional products for the Omaha Metro area including Ralston, Bellevue, Millard, Elkhorn, LaVista and Papillion.
about:
Corporate Creations was founded in 1995 in Omaha, Nebraska, by Wade Lewis while he was an undergraduate at the University of Nebraska at Omaha. Lewis initially launched Greek Creations to serve fraternity and sorority merchandise needs, and the business expanded into Corporate Creations after friends and family requested similar custom screen printing, embroidery, and promotional products for their own organizations.

The company provides custom screen printing, embroidery, and promotional product sourcing from its facility at 9001 F Street in Omaha. It offers access to over 700,000 custom printed products and handles orders with minimums of six pieces for embroidery, twelve for screen printing, and 100 for most promotional items. An in-house graphic design team prepares artwork, with proofs delivered within 48 hours and two revisions included.

Corporate Creations serves businesses, clubs, teams, churches, charities, schools, and non-profit organizations throughout the Omaha metro area, including Ralston, Bellevue, Millard, Elkhorn, La Vista, and Papillion. Customers range from local companies seeking branded apparel to university groups ordering Greek merchandise.

Lewis started the business to simplify how college groups purchased custom merchandise, and the company states its goal is to exceed expectations and turn every client into a repeat customer. It emphasizes low minimums, quick art approvals, and rush production options to meet tight deadlines.

name: Corporate Woodworking, Inc.
old_description: When your project involves custom architectural woodworking and requires the use of a firm that can deliver and install the highest quality product in the timeframe needed, Corporate Woodworking, Inc. (CWI) is the only choice. As one of the Andersen Companies, along with affiliate Andersen Interior Contracting, CWI operates with the same dedication to customer service and strong relationships that are the hallmark of any Dan Andersen owned business.
about:
Corporate Woodworking, Inc. (CWI) operates from Fairfield, New Jersey, as a Dan Andersen–owned business within the Andersen Companies group. Andersen founded the firm in 1989 after earlier ventures that began in his basement in 1974 and included the sale of The Andersen Corporation in 1986 and the launch of affiliate Andersen Interior Contracting.

The shop specializes in custom architectural woodworking and millwork, producing and installing reception desks, wall paneling with exotic veneers or lacquer finishes, door and sidelight systems, and pantry/café/servery millwork. The company reports fabricating thousands of square feet of paneling and thousands of door systems annually, coordinating appliance and equipment integration with hand‑crafted millwork.

CWI serves the commercial construction and architectural woodworking sectors, working with architects, designers, general contractors, and building owners on corporate office fit‑outs. Typical projects include high‑end reception areas, blueprint‑matched wall panels, complex door hardware coordination, and food‑service millwork that requires precise equipment alignment.

The firm cites its AWI Quality Certification Program (QCP) membership and the “Andersen Way” philosophy—emphasizing relationships, integrity, agility, teamwork, and efficiency—as differentiators. The approach aims to make CWI a partner that can adjust quickly to changing conditions while maintaining schedule and budget discipline.

name: Corteco USA
old_description: Welcome to Corteco, your premier spare parts supplier in the Independent Aftermarket. As a proud member of the global Freudenberg Group, we specialize in delivering components essential for optimal vehicle and machinery performance. With a comprehensive range of over 26,000 products, including sealing solutions, vibration control with rubber-metal parts, and premium cabin air filtration, we ensure OEM quality that exceeds industry standards.
about:
Corteco USA operates from Milan, Ohio, as the North American arm of the global Freudenberg Group. The company serves the independent automotive aftermarket with a portfolio that carries the Freudenberg engineering heritage, though a founding year for the U.S. entity is not publicly disclosed.

The supplier maintains a range of more than 26,000 spare parts organized into sealing solutions — including the Simmerring® oil seal — rubber-to-metal components for vibration control, steering and suspension kits numbering over 7,000 part numbers, and a cabin air filtration line with roughly 850 variations. Two brands, Corteco and TransTec, cover the lineup, supported by online tools such as the ecatcorteco.com catalog and the Findyourseal.com seal finder.

Customers include independent repair garages and distributors servicing passenger cars, heavy-duty trucks, two-wheelers, and emerging e-mobility platforms. The company positions its offering as original-equipment quality for the aftermarket channel.

Corteco traces its differentiation to the Freudenberg Group’s OEM manufacturing base, which it says allows the brand to deliver components that meet or exceed original specifications while providing digital procurement tools for faster part identification.

name: Country Pure Foods Corporate
old_description: Country Pure Foods is the premier manufacturer of beverages including
about:
Country Pure Foods is headquartered in Akron, Ohio. The company traces its origins to 1995, when a private equity firm merged two regional portion‑juice businesses, Ohio Pure Foods and Natural Country Farms, to form Country Pure Farms. In 2017 the company partnered with Blue Point Capital Partners LLC.

The company produces a broad line of portioned and multi‑serve juices, plant‑based beverages, and frozen novelties. It operates as a private‑label and co‑pack manufacturer serving foodservice, retail, and co‑pack markets. Through a series of acquisitions — including Ardmore Farms (1998), Vitality (2006), Cal Tex Citrus (2012), Quality Kitchens (2014), Ridgefield’s Brand Corp (2016), and Silver Springs Citrus (2017) — it has expanded production capacity across multiple U.S. facilities.

Its customers span foodservice (including restaurants, healthcare facilities, and K–12 schools), retail channels, and co‑pack partners. The company supplies portioned juice cups, cartons, juice boxes, and frozen products such as SideKicks to these segments.

Country Pure Foods positions itself as the largest supplier of portioned juice to the foodservice industry, emphasizing a broad product and packaging portfolio, national distribution, and a focus on private‑label and co‑pack solutions.

name: Craftco
old_description: Started as a job shop in 1981 by founders Billy and Marva Craft, Craftco has grown to become a nationwide leader in welding, manufacturing, materials handling, assembly and processing. We operate out of our 25,000-square-foot facility right here in Sheridan, Wyoming, and we take pride in building relationships and solving problems through customer service. Read about our services, capabilities, and even some of the products we build.
about:
Craftco began in 1981 as a one-person welding shop in Sheridan, Wyoming, founded by Billy and Marva Craft.

Today the company provides full-service manufacturing under one roof: welding and fabrication (including heavy plate forming, waterjet cutting, and certified structural welding), precision CNC machining (turning and milling up to 22-inch diameter), materials processing (raw stock management, precision sawing), coating and assembly (multi-layer protective coatings, sub-assembly, turnkey builds), and engineering and design (DFM analysis). The facility houses equipment such as a Marvel computerized band saw, a Flow water jet, a Mazak 7K laser cutter, and a Diamond BH 8525 press brake.

Craftco serves customers nationwide across mining, firearms manufacturing, fossil fuel extraction, robotics, commercial and residential construction, structural building, and oil and gas. Notable projects include wear liner plates for the Antofagasta mine in Chile (2012) and ongoing partnerships with large mining corporations and firearm manufacturers. The company also supports supply chain stability through blanket order and open PO programs.

The founders’ original focus on problem-solving remains central: Craftco positions itself as a manufacturing partner that combines engineering, machining, fabrication, and assembly to solve complex challenges. Its stated mission emphasizes long-term partnerships, quality, value, and professionalism, guided by a “Code of the West” ethos that stresses integrity, safety, and keeping promises.

name: Creative Composites Group, Augusta Molding Division
old_description: Creative Composites Group can help you advance your infrastructure projects beyond the limitations of traditional materials. We are the largest manufacturer of structural composites in the U.S. with innovative products across multiple industries.
about:
Creative Composites Group's Augusta Molding Division operates as Kenway Composites in Augusta, Maine. The division is part of the Creative Composites Group, a collection of U.S.-based structural composite manufacturers owned by Hill & Smith Holdings PLC, a UK-headquartered international group with divisions in Engineered Solutions, Roads & Security, and Galvanizing Services. No founding year or individual founders are disclosed for the Augusta operation; the group emphasizes decades of combined experience across its member companies.

The division produces fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites for structural applications, offering turnkey design-build, structural fabrication, manufacturing, engineering, and field services. Capabilities span custom FRP platforms, handrails, stairs, walkways, ladders, cage systems, tanks, towers, and linings, with production ranging from one-off molded fabrications to high-volume runs. The group's eight member companies—including Creative Pultrusions, Enduro Composites, and Composite Advantage—operate facilities across Pennsylvania, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas, and Maine, providing vertically integrated composite design and advanced manufacturing.

Primary markets include telecommunications and data centers, energy generation and distribution, marine, rail, and housing, as well as pulp and paper, water and wastewater treatment, and chemical storage. The company cites pulp mill washer system repairs and custom chemical storage tank installations as examples of its field service work, and notes that its engineering staff can deliver Professional Engineer-stamped blueprints for infrastructure projects.

Creative Composites Group positions itself as the largest U.S. manufacturer of structural composites, differentiating through vertical integration of multiple composite brands, in-house engineering, and over 60 years of collective FRP field service experience. The organization states it was formed to combine the expertise of its member companies to deliver engineered composite systems that are lightweight, corrosion-resistant, and long-lasting for infrastructure projects of any scope.
